verdict.rationale: Airbyte's core design moves data into destinations the user controls (data warehouses/lakes/DBs) in standard schemas, and offers a self-hostable OSS core (abctl, Kubernetes, OSS quickstart) plus 600+ connectors, supporting data portability and avoiding platform lock-in. However, community evidence disputes the 'fully open source' framing (paywalled security/enterprise features) and reports real friction self-hosting, which tempers confidence in a clean 'export and leave' story. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of exporting Airbyte's own metadata/config in open formats, independent verification of destination data portability, and resolution of the community claim that parts of the platform are not truly open.
